Assume ALL firearms are loaded. Keep the safety on if you're not firing. Keep the firearm pointed downward after you've emptied it and before firing. Keep your finger off of the trigger until you're ready to fire at your target after you've acquired aim. Also, if you're shooting a pistol line up the dots assuring that there is no excessive space between your back sights and front sights. They should be perfectly aligned. If you're going to do a follow up shot on a target (say a few shots to the head or chest) aim a little lower due to muzzle climb. If you're planning on doing multiple successive shots understand you're not going to hit your target perfectly each time because of muzzle climb. This is why you aim lower. Also keep your finger just slightly over the trigger and work on improving your trigger pull. You can pull back on the slide (the top of a pistol) to ensure one is in the chamber. If you pull the trigger and the weapon does not fire but you hear the hammer or pin striking the bullet quickly aim the weapon at the ground or down range for at least a minute and wait to see if the bullet ejects (this is called a squib fire)If you're at an indoor range this shouldn't be a problem but outdoors; do not, I repeat DO NOT stay on the firing line when someone calls for a cease fire.
